questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.topic: The Maclaurin series for cosine
questions.learningObjective: Identify the Maclaurin series for cosine
questions.stem: In the kitchen of a small trattoria, the chef expands the cosine of an angle in radians to check a garnish timing curve. Which series belongs on the costing sheet?

options.text: cos(x) = 1 - x²/2! + x⁴/4! - x⁶/6! + …, using even powers with alternating signs
cos(x) = 1 + x²/2! + x⁴/4! + x⁶/6! + …, using even powers with all positive signs
options.misconception: believes every even-power term of cosine carries a plus sign

options.text: cos(x) = 1 - x + x²/2! - x³/3! + x⁴/4! - …, using every power of x
options.misconception: confuses cosine with the alternating exponential series

options.text: cos(x) = 1 - x²/2 + x⁴/4 - x⁶/8 + …, using ordinary powers in the denominators
options.misconception: treats the factorial denominators as simple doubling powers

questions.explanation: The cosine series keeps only even powers, alternating signs, and factorial denominators. Option B drops the alternation, option C is the exponential series, and option D drops the factorials.
questions.hint: Check the first four derivatives at zero.

options.text: The series terms shrink without bound for large x, so the formula must hold for every real x
options.misconception: treats term sizes as proof of convergence everywhere

options.text: At x = 2 the partial sums oscillate and fail to approach arctan(2) of about 1.107
The series has no odd powers of x, so it cannot represent arctangent values away from zero
options.misconception: confuses missing even powers with a failure of the odd-power series

options.text: The series needs a constant term of 1 to match the value arctan(0) of zero

questions.explanation: The arctangent series converges only for |x| ≤ 1 and diverges for larger |x|, so evaluating it at 2 cannot produce arctan(2) of about 1.107. Missing even powers and a zero constant term are normal here.
questions.hint: Compare the growth of the terms with the size of x.
